feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: A new global report finds climate change behind most of the world's heat deaths
entry.summary: The Lancet Countdown's 2026 global report finds heat linked to an average of 540,800 deaths a year from 2016 to 2023, with 68 percent attributed to climate change. — Sources: The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change, 2026 global report (10th edition), published 27 October 2026

entry.title: The Rhine at Kaub, Germany, held steady at its recovery high
entry.summary: Germany's federal gauge network measured the Rhine at Kaub at 56 centimetres for a second consecutive day, unchanged from yesterday, after three days of recovery from the river's drought low. — Sources: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung, Pegelonline gauge network, direct reading, 28 October 2026

entry.title: Singapore's haze held in the moderate band for a third consecutive day
entry.summary: Singapore's National Environment Agency recorded a 24-hour PSI of 67 to 79 across all five regions at 1pm local time, moderate everywhere for a third day running, though the readings rose compared with the previous two days. — Sources: National Environment Agency, Singapore, direct reading, 28 October 2026, 1pm SGT

entry.title: A new global report finds climate-linked health harms accelerating since the Paris Agreement
entry.summary: The Lancet Countdown's 10th annual global report finds that climate-linked health risks and harms grew faster in the decade since the Paris Agreement than in the decade before it, with 68 percent of the world's average annual heat deaths from 2016 to 2023 attributed to climate change. — Sources: The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change, 2026 global report (10th edition), published 27 October 2026

entry.title: Heat cost the global economy over a trillion dollars in lost work in 2025, a new report finds
entry.summary: The Lancet Countdown's 2026 global report puts 2025's heat-driven loss to the global economy at approximately 1.07 trillion dollars in lost labour productivity. — Sources: The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change, 2026 global report (10th edition), published 27 October 2026
